_comment: chirp ground (NFM) daemon defaults. Phase 4a defaults + Phase 4b 'sdr' block. Separate UDP port + state path + hit log + icecast fallback from airband so the two daemons can coexist. See chirp/config/README.md. GMRS 2026-11-08: channel_bw_hz is pinned here. It is NOT a channel width -- it is the one-sided cutoff handed to firdes.low_pass() in chirp/dsp/channel.py, so the demod passband is 2x this number. The inherited default 12500.0 therefore built a 25 kHz-wide filter on the 12.5 kHz GMRS grid: a single key-up on 462.5625 landed at roughly the -6 dB passband edge of both neighbours and opened them too, so one transmission showed up as a run of ~10 hits and the priority gate had a 9-in-10 chance of latching an off-tune channel (audible as static). 8000.0 keeps wideband GMRS intact -- Carson 2*(5 kHz dev + 3 kHz audio) = 16 kHz, i.e. +-8 kHz -- while putting the 12.5 kHz neighbour 4 kHz deep into the stopband. Do not raise this to 'cover the channel'; airband sets 6000.0 for the same reason. SQUELCH 2026-11-08: global_squelch_dbfs is -61.0, NOT the -56.0 this file shipped with. -56.0 was measurably too tight. A real station on 462.5500 (GMRS 15, almost certainly an automatic repeater identifier) keys a 9.14 s +-0.25 burst every 30 minutes -- 103 logged events from 2026-09-21 to 2026-11-08 -- at median -56.94 dBFS, so 84 of 103 bursts fall BELOW -56.0 and raising squelch to -56.0 at 08:27:11 silenced it within one cycle. Detection at -61.0 is ~98% of those bursts versus ~18% at -56.0. The reason -56.0 looked necessary was two other bugs now fixed: a 25 kHz-wide demod filter on a 12.5 kHz grid (see channel_bw_hz above) and a priority gate that chose by string hash instead of signal level, which together made one transmission look like ten and sound like static. With those fixed, squelch no longer has to paper over them. Do not raise this to quieten a multi-hit run: a run spanning >25 kHz is front-end overload from a near-field transmitter and squelch cannot fix it.

sdr._comment: SDR source defaults for ground. Revision 5.0 (Neptune, 2026-10-12): ground NFM runs on RSP1B serial 240526DE60 via SoapySDR, NOT the RTL. Revision 4.0 said RTL 61108285 and that is now wrong twice over -- no RTL is attached to Neptune at all (ioreg shows only the two SDRplay serials 240526DE60 and 180903EF32), and the deployed service does not read this value anyway: ~/.config/sb3/chirp-ground.env sets CHIRP_SDR_DEVICE_ARGS, which overrides the config exactly as chirp-airband.env does on scannerbox-1. This key is kept correct so it is not actively misleading. TWO THINGS MUST BE TRUE or chirp hangs in source-open and never binds its command port, looking like a crash loop with no traceback: (1) SOAPY_SDR_PLUGIN_PATH must point at the SoapySDR module dir (/opt/homebrew/lib/SoapySDR/modules0.8) -- without it SoapySDR loads no sdrplay module and finds zero devices even though libsdrPlaySupport.so is on disk; (2) the SDRplay API service must not be wedged -- when it is, SoapySDRUtil --find hangs forever and so does chirp. 'sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.sdrplay.service' clears it. center_freq_hz 162.475 MHz is the marine/WX band; the LO scheduler retunes per cluster.
